Mark the student's response to a question from Riverview Task 1 2013 (a Riverview Year 12 Business Studies assessment, Operations topic) strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting.

Question 3(c) [3 marks]: Define the term warranty and explain ONE potential benefit to a company that decides to issue one.
STIMULUS / CASE INFORMATION:
Wong Tong Noodle Bar Pty Ltd is a restaurant that has made a decision to cook their meals directly in front of the customer rather than behind kitchen doors. They believe that they might develop a competitive advantage over their competitors using this approach.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 3):
2 marks: Shows cause and effect relating to the benefits of a warranty for the business
1 marks: Provides an accurate definition of the term warranty


ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
A warranty is a legally binding guarantee that a product meets certain standards; if it fails, the business repairs or replaces it free of charge. Benefits: convincing customers to select your product because of a more comprehensive warranty than competitors (a differentiator); feedback on the quality of production that allows the business to improve quality and gain a reputational advantage, leading to improved sales longer term.

TEACHER MARKER COMMENTS:
Most students could define warranty, but some talked about the benefits to customers rather than to the business as the question asked.
